note: Archive Chess maps each chess role to a god of the chosen pantheon; capturing a piece reveals a fact about that god. Every fact is grounded in a real chapter — 'basis' must appear in that pantheon's chapter (checked by tools/verify-chess.js). Roles: K Q R B N P.

K.basis: Zeus became king of a new order
K.fact: Zeus overthrew the Titans and became king of a new order, the Olympians.

Q.fact: Athena, goddess of wisdom and war, is known in art by her owl, aegis, and olive.

R.fact: Poseidon, lord of the sea and earthquakes, was worshipped among the Olympians from the Bronze Age on.

B.fact: At Delphi the priestess of Apollo, the Pythia, delivered the god's oracles to all of Greece.

N.fact: Ares, god of war, stood among the twelve Olympians of the Greek pantheon.

P.fact: The Eleusinian Mysteries near Athens promised initiates a happier lot beyond death than the grey shades of Hades.

K.basis: Osiris eventually became the god through whom every Egyptian
K.fact: Osiris — a good king murdered by his brother Set — became the god through whom every Egyptian hoped to live again.

Q.basis: the concept of truth, balance, cosmic order, and justice
Q.fact: Ma'at was at once a goddess and the concept of truth, balance, cosmic order, and justice, which the pharaoh existed to uphold.

R.basis: Ra crossed the sky by day in his solar barque
R.fact: Ra crossed the sky by day in his solar barque and each night fought the chaos-serpent Apep so that dawn could come.

B.basis: the ibis-headed Thoth, scribe of the gods
B.fact: The ibis-headed Thoth, scribe of the gods, stood ready to record the verdict at the weighing of the heart.

N.fact: The jackal-headed Anubis steadies the scales of judgment — and, myth said, embalmed Osiris to make the first mummy.

P.fact: The six parts of the Eye of Horus doubled as fractions — 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and on — used to measure grain.

K.basis: god of war and death, but also of poetry
K.fact: Odin, chief of the gods, is god of war and death but also of poetry, prophecy, and the runes he won hanging nine nights on the world-tree.

Q.basis: goddess of love, gold, and battle-slain
Q.fact: Freyja was goddess of love, gold, and the battle-slain — she takes half the dead — and mistress of seidr.

R.fact: At the center of the Norse cosmos stands Yggdrasil, the world-tree, an immense ash whose roots and branches hold the worlds together.

B.fact: Baldr, the beautiful and beloved god whose death Loki engineers, is the first casualty on the road to Ragnarok.

N.basis: the thunder-god, defender of gods and humans against the giants
N.fact: Thor, the thunder-god, defends gods and humans against the giants with his hammer Mjolnir.

P.fact: The battle-slain were welcomed to Odin's hall of Valhalla, to feast and fight until the last day.
